description: Eleven HCP Young Adult subjects: sub-100307, the subject the package brief's acceptance test names, and ten drawn at random (seed 0), five women and five men, from the 946 with complete SBCI pipeline output in the lab's copy. One SC file per subject with its streamline endpoints, rebuilt on the ico4 grid by tools/build_hcp_cohort.py --layout young-adult. Sex and the open-access age band come from the HCP's open-access data; no FC yet. Redistributed under the WU-Minn HCP Open Access Data Use Terms (DATA_USE.txt in the folder).

SBCI example cohort: eleven HCP Young Adult subjects
====================================================

These files are structural continuous connectomes on the fsaverage ico4 grid
(5,124 vertices), with each subject's streamline endpoints, in the format of the
sbci Python package (https://github.com/xya2001/SBCI). They were derived from
data of the WU-Minn Human Connectome Project (HCP Young Adult) through the lab's
SBCI pipeline output and rebuilt with tools/build_hcp_cohort.py --layout
young-adult. `sbci download hcp-ya` fetches and verifies them.

They are redistributed under the WU-Minn HCP Consortium Open Access Data Use
Terms, which apply to anyone who downloads them:
https://www.humanconnectome.org/study/hcp-young-adult/document/wu-minn-hcp-consortium-open-access-data-use-terms

In short, by using these files you agree to those terms, among them: not to
attempt to identify or contact any subject; to comply with your institution's
rules for research on human subjects; to redistribute these data, or anything
derived from them, only under the same terms; and to acknowledge the HCP in any
public presentation of results, with this wording:

  "Data were provided [in part] by the Human Connectome Project, WU-Minn
  Consortium (Principal Investigators: David Van Essen and Kamil Ugurbil;
  1U54MH091657) funded by the 16 NIH Institutes and Centers that support the
  NIH Blueprint for Neuroscience Research; and by the McDonnell Center for
  Systems Neuroscience at Washington University."

The terms page above is authoritative; this note only points to it.
